learning_objective: 🎯 Witness the magic of the free market! See how the invisible forces of demand and supply interact to determine the exact price and quantity of goods.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Market equilibrium is the point where Quantity Demanded exactly equals Quantity Supplied. Geometrically, it's the exact point where the downward-sloping Demand curve intersects the upward-sloping Supply curve.
If the price is set below equilibrium, buyers want more than sellers are willing to produce. This creates a shortage (excess demand). Buyers compete, driving the price back up to equilibrium.
If the price is above equilibrium, sellers produce more than buyers want. This creates a surplus (excess supply). Unsold stock piles up, forcing sellers to lower the price back to equilibrium.

Price Ceiling: A legal maximum price (e.g., rent control or essential medicines) set below equilibrium, causing shortages. Price Floor: A legal minimum price (e.g., Minimum Support Price for farmers) set above equilibrium, causing surpluses.

fun_activity.title: 🎫 The Concert Ticket Hustle
fun_activity.instructions: A famous singer is coming to town. Tickets are priced at ₹1000 (below equilibrium). The website crashes because 50,000 people want to buy, but there are only 10,000 seats. This is Excess Demand! That's why tickets immediately end up on the black market for ₹5000 (the true equilibrium price).

exam_tips: 📌 When both Demand and Supply shift in the same direction, you can predict the change in Quantity, but the change in Price depends on the magnitude of the shifts.
📌 A Price Ceiling always leads to a shortage and black marketing. A Price Floor always leads to a surplus and requires government procurement (buying the excess).
📌 An increase in income shifts the demand curve to the right for normal goods, raising both equilibrium price and quantity.
quick_recap: ⭐ Adam Smith called the free market mechanism the 'Invisible Hand'.
⭐ When demand increases (shifts right) and supply is perfectly elastic, only quantity increases while price remains constant.
⭐ Viable industry means the demand and supply curves intersect in the positive quadrant; non-viable means they never intersect at a positive price.
